4,532 likes, 334 comments - drsnehal_adsule on December 15, 2025: "For a long time, I felt behind.
Behind people my age.
Behind the life I imagined.
Behind timelines that society silently expects us to follow.

It seemed like everyone else was moving forward
while I was standing still, just trying to breathe.

What I know now is this…

There is no universal timeline.
No invisible checklist you’re failing at.
No age by which life must make sense.

If life slowed you down,
it wasn’t to punish you.
It was to make you listen.
To heal parts of you that had been hurting quietly for years.

Healing is messy.
It’s not aesthetic. 
It doesn’t always look strong.

And that doesn’t mean you’re losing.
It means you’re doing the bravest work of your life.

If you’re in a hard season right now.. keep going.
I promise you.. the view changes.
You change.
And one day you’ll look back and realize how far you’ve come.

You are not behind anyone.
You are not behind life.

You are exactly where you need to be
to become who you’re meant to be🦋

Today, on my birthday,
I choose patience over pressure.
Trust over timelines.
Hope over fear.

Here’s to surviving the hard years
and slowly becoming someone you’re proud of🥂

Happy birthday to me💜".

2,505 likes, 505 comments - drsnehal_adsule on December 28, 2025: "Most women don’t need “more discipline”.
They don’t need to “try harder”.

They simply need clarity.

Because your body is not confusing.
It is constantly communicating with you.

Fatigue that doesn’t go away…
Hairfall that scares you…
Weight that refuses to move…
Periods that are irregular or painful…
Mood swings, anxiety, bloating, PCOS…

None of this is “random”.
None of this is “normal for every woman”.

Most of the time…
There is a reason.
There is a root cause.
And when you understand that…
Healing becomes easier.

That’s why I created this post for you.
Not to scare you.
Not to overwhelm you.
But to help you finally understand what your body may be trying to tell you.

Because when you test right…
You diagnose right…
You heal right.

And you can finally feel better in your body. 💛

If this helped you understand your body better…
Save this post.
Share it with a woman who needs answers😊

And comment “2026” if you want 2026 to be the year you actually understand and heal your body… not just “manage” it 💛".

108 likes, 1 comments - drsnehal_adsule on October 6, 2026: "Some of my slightly cringe little rituals that have helped me stay consistent with food for years 😂

And honestly, none of them are complicated.

The first one is probably the most boring:

My breakfast is almost the same every single day.

Two eggs + one slice of bread.

Because I genuinely don’t want to make food decisions before 9 a.m. 😂

On days I can’t have eggs, I’ll have poha because it’s my favourite.

I’ve realised that having a few “default meals” takes away so much decision-making.

I don’t wake up thinking, “What should I eat today?”

I already know.

The second one is my warm water ritual.

The moment I wake up, I have warm water.

I’ve been doing this for almost 7 years now.

And honestly, it’s less about the water and more about what it represents for me.

It’s the first little thing I do every morning that tells my brain, “I’m taking care of myself today.”

That feeling of starting my day right makes it easier for me to continue making good choices through the day.

And yes, I also find it comforting for my tummy.

The third one is something I started doing when I’m eating around other people.

I don’t put a huge portion on my plate.

I serve myself a little, eat slowly, and if I’m actually still hungry, I can always take more.

Because I’ve noticed that when there’s a lot of food sitting in front of me, I’m much more likely to mindlessly finish it just because it’s there.

And there’s another funny psychological trick here.

I’ve kind of created an identity for myself around food: I’m not someone who hogs.

So when I’m at a restaurant or eating with people, I naturally become more mindful about how much I’m eating.

It sounds silly.

But these tiny rituals have helped me more than trying to be “disciplined” all the time.

Because consistency isn’t about making the perfect choice every day.

It’s about creating little systems that make the right choice easier.

If you want me to help you create a simple Desi fat-loss routine that you can actually follow in your real life, comment PLAN below…

I’ll send you the details in the DMs💜".

131 likes, 57 comments - drsnehal_adsule on September 21, 2026: "PCOS is not simply weight gain + infertility.

It can show up very differently from one woman to another. Irregular periods, acne, excess facial hair, hair fall, cravings, fatigue, insulin resistance and changes in mood or body image can all be part of the picture.

And no, you don’t need to have every symptom to have PCOS.

The important part is understanding what’s actually going on in your body instead of trying random “PCOS fixes” from Instagram.

Want a simple guide to understanding PCOS/PCOD and what you can actually work on?

149 likes, 197 comments - drsnehal_adsule on September 18, 2026: "You’re eating the same way, trying the same things, but suddenly…

Your periods feel different.
Your sleep isn’t as restful.
Your mood feels all over the place.
Cravings are stronger.
You feel more tired than usual.
And the weight that once came off easily now feels SO much harder to lose.

But please don’t respond by simply eating less. 🫶🏻

Start by going back to the basics your body needs:

✨ Protein: Add a proper protein source to every main meal. Think dal, eggs, chicken, fish, paneer, curd or tofu.

✨ Strength training: Aim for 2–3 sessions a week. Building and maintaining muscle becomes increasingly important as we get older.

✨ Sleep: Try to keep your sleep and wake-up time consistent. Your body loves rhythm more than perfection.

✨ Stress: If you’re constantly juggling work, family, responsibilities and everyone else’s needs, your mental load matters too.

✨ Track your symptoms: Don’t look at the weighing scale alone. Notice changes in your periods, sleep, energy, mood, cravings and digestion.

And one important thing…

Not every symptom is “just hormones.”

If a change is new, severe, unusual or persistent, talk to your doctor and get it checked rather than assuming you simply need to “try harder.”

Your body isn’t failing you❤️

You may simply need a different approach for the body you have today, not the body you had 10 years ago.

I’ve put together a simple 3-Day Hormone & Mind Reboot Guide to help you understand where to start without overwhelming yourself.

👇 Comment RESET and I’ll send it to you.".

145 likes, 469 comments - drsnehal_adsule on September 13, 2026: "If you read that list and thought, “That’s literally me”, this is for you.

I see so many women in their 30s stuck in the same cycle.

They lose 5 kg.
Then life happens and they gain it back.

They start cutting carbs.
Then the cravings become impossible to control.

They skip meals during the day.
Then they are starving and snacking at night.

They start exercising.
Then one busy week throws everything off.

They feel tired all the time.
So they rely on chai or coffee to get through the day.

Then they notice more hair fall, dull skin, bloating and stubborn belly fat.

And slowly, they start thinking:

“Maybe my metabolism is slow.”

“Maybe this is just what happens after 30.”

“Maybe I just need more willpower.”

But please don’t reduce everything to weight.

If your body is feeling different, look at the bigger picture.

How much protein are you actually eating?

Are your meals keeping you full?

Are you eating enough fibre?

Are you going hours without food and then struggling with cravings at night?

Are you sleeping well?

Are you constantly stressed?

Are you moving regularly, or only exercising when you are trying to lose weight?

How is your digestion?

Has your period or cycle changed?

And if you have persistent hair fall or fatigue, have you actually looked into the possible causes instead of just starting another supplement?

You do not need to completely change your life.

You do not need to stop eating roti and rice.

You do not need to survive on salads.

You do not need to start another extreme diet every Monday.

You need to understand what your body needs and build habits you can actually maintain.

Because losing the same 5 kg every year is not the goal.

Feeling energetic, nourished, strong, comfortable in your body and being able to maintain a healthy weight is the goal.

If you are a woman in your 30s and you relate to this, I made my FREE Healthy Woman Blueprint to help you understand the key foundations you should be looking at for your health.

DM me “HEALTHY” and I’ll send it to you for FREE💜".
